one_month_reasoning: Avnet's own Q1 FY27 report most likely falls just outside the window: the quarter ends 2026-10-03 (a week later than last year's Sep 27 close, which was reported Oct 29), and MarketBeat estimates the date at about Nov 4. No date had been announced as of today. Inside the window are read-across events: Texas Instruments and other analog/MCU suppliers report in mid-to-late October, Arrow reports Q3 around late October, and memory price updates come out. All of these move distributors. If Avnet does report before Nov 1, the bar is high: Q1 guidance is $2.80-2.90 and the stock has doubled. I centre the distribution on today's $106.94 with no drift. The stock closed at an all-time high, up 4.6% on the day, so momentum and short-term reversal roughly cancel. Monthly vol is ~11.5%, slightly above the 37%/3.5 = 10.6% rule because of the peer-earnings read-across.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods: forward P/E (~$12 NTM EPS at Oct-2027 x 9x = $108, weight 0.5); mid-cycle earnings power ($7.5 x 13x = $97, weight 0.3); and a historical peak-cycle multiple on the Q1 FY27 run-rate ($11.40 x 6.5x = $74, weight 0.2). Result is about $98.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS as of Oct-2027 ~$12.0 x 9.0x

inputs_detail.derivation: Q1 guidance annualizes to $11.40. Arrow says its backlog extends into 1H27 and book-to-bill is above 1, which supports modest further growth. Consensus FY28 of $11.22 looks stale against the run-rate, so I use ~5% above the run-rate and stop there because NAND loosens in 2H27 (source 8).

AVT currently trades at 10.3x forward consensus. In the 2022-23 peak it traded at 4.6-6x trailing EPS ($36-50 on $7.86-8.26). Arrow's 5-year P/E range is 4.3-15.5x. One year further into the upcycle I expect some compression toward the peak-cycle norm, but not all the way, given AI/data-center exposure of 10-15%.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Mid-cycle earnings power: $30B sales x 3.5% adj op margin = $1.05B, less ~$230M interest, 23% tax, 84M shares = ~$7.5 EPS, x 13x mid-cycle P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: Sits between FY26 sales of $27.6B and the Q1 FY27 guidance run-rate of ~$36.6B.
Q4 FY26 adj op margin was 3.8% (EC 4.1%, Farnell 9.0%), and FY26 GAAP margin was 2.6%. I take a mid-cycle value slightly below the current quarter.
Debt ~$3.2B at ~7% all-in. Tax is the midpoint of the 21-25% guided range.
Guided 85M, less ongoing buybacks ($138M in FY26).
Normalized-earnings multiples for distributors sit around 10-15x. Arrow's 5-year average is 9.6x on mixed earnings and its high is 15.5x, so 13x is a mid-cycle value.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Peak-cycle base rate: Q1 FY27 run-rate $11.40 x 6.5x

inputs_detail.derivation: In 2022-23 AVT topped out near $50-51 with FY23 EPS of $8.26 (~6x). Its P/E low was 4.6x in Oct-2022. The 2018 peak was also around $49. I use 6.5x.

bear.story: The cycle peaks in mid-2027, as it typically does about 18-24 months after the trough. NAND supply loosens in 2H27, price-driven revenue reverses, and a 2027 US recession (Kalshi ~41%) hits industrial demand. Working capital that consumed cash in FY26 becomes a problem. The market applies the historical ~6x peak multiple to ~$11 EPS, giving about $65.

base.story: Earnings keep rising to about a $12-13 run-rate through FY27, helped by backlog into 1H27, but the market starts to price late-cycle risk and the multiple compresses from ~10x to ~8.5-9x forward. The stock ends roughly flat.

bull.story: The AI and memory supercycle runs into 2028, with DRAM tight through 2027 per TrendForce. EPS reaches a $14-15 run-rate with operating leverage, and the market treats this as a structurally longer cycle at ~10x.

thesis_break_reason: At about $70 the stock would trade at ~6x the Q1 FY27 run-rate EPS. That is the multiple the market paid at the 2018 and 2022-23 cycle tops. Trading there would most likely mean the market has concluded that earnings have peaked, through order cancellations, book-to-bill below 1, falling memory prices or a recession, rather than ordinary volatility. It is also a ~35% drop, almost a 1-sigma-plus move against 37% vol.

key_uncertainties: How long the cycle lasts: whether AI/data-center and memory demand make this upcycle longer than the usual ~2-year distributor cycle
How much revenue comes from price rather than units (Arrow says ~1/3 of sequential growth is price) and how fast that reverses
Working capital: FY26 operating cash flow was -$281M with $6.1B of inventory; a quick downturn could leave Avnet holding excess inventory
Macro and recession timing in 2027, plus tariff policy on semiconductors
Whether the market keeps paying ~10x forward or reverts to the historical ~6x peak-cycle multiple
reasoning: Avnet (electronic components distributor) has doubled in a year on a sharp upcycle. Q4 FY26 sales were $8.3B (+48% y/y) with adj EPS of $2.28. Q1 FY27 guidance is $9.15B and $2.85, an ~$11.40 annualized run-rate, so the stock trades at ~9.4x run-rate and ~10.3x consensus FY27 EPS (~$10.45). Base rates from AVT's own history argue for caution. Through 2016-2025 the stock never held above ~$55 in any cycle. At the 2018 and 2022-23 earnings peaks it traded at only ~4.6-6.5x peak EPS (FY23 EPS $8.26 vs a ~$50 high), and in the downturn that followed, EPS fell 34% in FY24. Distributor upcycles typically last ~6-8 quarters from trough. This one turned around 2H calendar 2025, so the 12-month window likely includes the peak and early signs of a turn. Against that, peers and the trade press point to a longer runway. Arrow's backlog extends into 1H27 with book-to-bill above 1 in all regions. TrendForce sees DRAM tight through 2027 and the memory peak in 2027, with NAND loosening in 2H27. AVT's AI/data-center exposure is up to 10-15%. The market is already paying above historical peak multiples, which leaves room for both compression and further upside. Macro: Kalshi prices a 2027 US recession at ~41% (via simplefunctions aggregator; volume not retrievable, as the page returned 503), which is a meaningful left tail for an industrial-heavy distributor. My blended fair value is ~$98, below the $107 price. The probability-weighted scenario mean is ~$106 and the median ~$101-102. The ladder is a lognormal around a ~$102 median with ~37% vol, plus a fatter left tail for cycle-peak de-rating (P(<75) ~24%). Research was limited: macrotrends, fullratio and the Kalshi aggregator blocked fetching, so their historical P/E and market figures come from search-result snippets, which I cross-checked against Twelve Data monthly prices. Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimate endpoints were unavailable because of plan and rate limits.
